Robust-Bayes inference for set-identified proxy-SVARs (Giacomini, Kitagawa & Read)

Source: R/psvar-bayes-full.R
varm_proxy_gkr.Rd

Prior-robust Bayesian inference on impulse responses in a proxy-SVAR identified by exogeneity of r proxies plus (optional) sign restrictions, following Giacomini, Kitagawa & Read (2022, J. Econometrics) who build on Giacomini & Kitagawa (2021, Econometrica). Write the SVAR in orthogonal-reduced form \(y_t=Bx_t+\Sigma_{tr}Q\varepsilon_t\) and the first stage \(m_t=Dy_t+Gx_t+\sum_l H_lm_{t-l}+v_t\). The reduced-form parameters \(\phi=(B,\Sigma,D,G,H,\Upsilon)\) are updated by the data; the rotation \(Q\) is not. The identifying restrictions are the exogeneity restrictions \(D\Sigma_{tr}q_j=0\) for the first \(K-r\) shocks (the proxies are correlated with the last r shocks), the user's sign restrictions \(S(\phi,Q)\ge0\) and the sign normalisation \(\mathrm{diag}(Q'\Sigma_{tr}^{-1})\ge0\). Instead of one prior for \(Q|\phi\), GKR consider all priors supported on the set \(\mathcal{Q}(\phi)\) of admissible rotations; this gives, for each \(\phi\), bounds \([l(\phi),u(\phi)]\) of the response, and

  • the set of posterior means \([E_\phi l(\phi),\,E_\phi u(\phi)]\), a consistent estimator of the identified set under strong proxies (GKR sec. 2.4), averaged over draws with a non-empty set;

  • the robust credible region of level \(\alpha\): the shortest interval that has posterior probability \(\ge\alpha\) under every prior in the class, centred at \(\arg\min_\eta \hat z_\alpha(\eta)\) with radius \(\min_\eta\hat z_\alpha(\eta)\), where \(\hat z_\alpha(\eta)\) is the \(\alpha\)-quantile over draws of \(\max\{|\eta-l|,|\eta-u|\}\);

  • the posterior probability that the identified set is non-empty (plausibility of the sign restrictions).

The bounds are approximated with GKR's Algorithm 2 (Steps 2.1-2.3 and 3'): per reduced-form draw, up to nq rotations satisfying all restrictions are drawn and the extremes taken. This underestimates the identified set at each draw (converging as nq grows); GKR's constrained-optimiser Algorithm 1 is not implemented. With size set, Algorithm 3 is used (responses to a unit shock to target; bounds may be unbounded if the impact on target can be near zero). lower/upper of a point-identified shock (e.g. the proxy shock when r = 1) coincide, and the set of posterior means then equals the posterior mean of the point-identified response. The single-prior posterior implied by the first accepted rotation of each draw (the conventional Bayesian answer, GKR recommend reporting it too) is returned as draws/bands.

Usage

varm_proxy_gkr(
  fit,
  m,
  signs = NULL,
  shock = NULL,
  target = 1L,
  size = NULL,
  pm = 0L,
  horizon = 20L,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  ndraw = NULL,
  nq = 100L,
  maxtry = 2000L,
  sign_horizon = 1L
)

Arguments

fit

a bvarm() object (class bvarm).

m

proxy: numeric vector, or T x r matrix of r proxies, aligned with the data (the first p rows are dropped to match the residuals).

signs

sign restrictions on all shocks: K x K matrix or K x K x H array of +1/-1/0 (rows variables, columns shocks; the last r columns are the proxy shocks), or NULL.

shock

column (shock) whose responses are bounded; default K (the last proxy shock).

target

variable(s) (name or position) whose impact response is normalised to size; length r.

size

NULL for responses to a one-standard-deviation shock (GKR default), or the impact on target (single value) for responses to a unit shock (Algorithm 3).

pm

number of lags of the proxy in the first-stage regression.

horizon

maximum horizon (impact is 0).

level

credibility levels of the robust credible regions.

ndraw

number of posterior draws to use (default: all stored draws).

nq

accepted rotations per reduced-form draw used for the bounds.

maxtry

rotation draws attempted per reduced-form draw before declaring the set empty.

sign_horizon

number of horizons (from impact) over which a matrix signs is imposed.

Value

a varm_proxy_gkr object: lower, upper (set of posterior means, (H+1) x K), region ((H+1) x K x 2*length(level), robust credible region limits ordered like bands), prob_nonempty, lu (list l, u of (H+1) x K x M arrays over draws with non-empty set), draws/bands (single-prior posterior, shock column only), and metadata.

Details

The reduced-form prior is the one in fit for \((B,\Sigma)\) (e.g. Minnesota) and Jeffreys for the first stage (GKR sec. 4.1.1 use independent Jeffreys priors; the NIW prior of bvarm() also fits their framework). Frequentist coverage is claimed by GKR only for strong proxies (their sec. 3: with a weak proxy the Bernstein-von Mises property fails and the set of posterior means need not be consistent). Check proxy_fstat(). The conditioning number of \(D\Sigma_{tr}\) diagnostic of their sec. 4.1.6 is not computed.

References

Giacomini, R., Kitagawa, T. and Read, M. (2022). Robust Bayesian inference in proxy SVARs. Journal of Econometrics 228(1), 107-126.

Giacomini, R. and Kitagawa, T. (2021). Robust Bayesian inference for set-identified models. Econometrica 89(4), 1519-1556.

See also

varm_proxy_arw(), varm_proxy_robust() (frequentist weak-instrument-robust sets)

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
e <- matrix(rnorm(900), 300)
y <- matrix(0, 300, 3)
for (t in 2:300) y[t, ] <- 0.4 * y[t - 1, ] + e[t, ] %*% t(matrix(c(1, .3, .2, 0, 1, .4, .5, .2, 1), 3))
bf <- bvarm(y, p = 1, ndraw = 200, nburn = 100)
S <- matrix(0, 3, 3); S[1, 1] <- 1; S[2, 1] <- 1   # shock 1 raises variables 1 and 2 on impact
varm_proxy_gkr(bf, m = e[, 3] + rnorm(300, sd = 0.5), signs = S, shock = 1, horizon = 6, nq = 50)
#> <varm_proxy_gkr> robust-Bayes bounds, shock 1 (1 proxy; 1 s.d. shock), horizon 0..6
#> 200 reduced-form draws, nq = 50; P(identified set non-empty) = 1
#> set of posterior means [lower, upper] and 90% robust credible region:
#> y1:
#>     lower upper rcr_lo rcr_hi
#> h=0 0.285 1.027  0.185  1.097
#> h=4 0.014 0.043 -0.011  0.071
#> y2:
#>      lower upper rcr_lo rcr_hi
#> h=0  0.030 1.005  0.000  1.061
#> h=4 -0.004 0.061 -0.037  0.099
#> y3:
#>      lower upper rcr_lo rcr_hi
#> h=0  0.060 0.438  0.015  0.488
#> h=4 -0.007 0.011 -0.041  0.033
# }
